entries.text: markoto syncs every keystroke live, open the same link on a second device or send it to a collaborator and their edits arrive on your screen the moment they hit a key. The avatars at the top show who else is in the doc; the coloured ring on a passage shows where their cursor is.
You're the only one in the doc, for now
You see one avatar in the topbar, yours. Type freely; the cursor is yours; the doc is yours.

entries.caption: You start a draft. Top-right: just your avatar. Nobody else here yet.

entries.text: Sam joins via the share link
You send Sam the URL. Sam logs in on their own browser, opens the link, and lands in the same doc, separate identity, separate session, same content.

entries.caption: Sam lands in the doc. Both avatars show in the topbar, Sam at the front (themselves), Maya right next to them.

entries.text: Sam types: you see it land in real time

Sam adds a paragraph. On your screen the characters appear at Sam's cursor a fraction of a second after Sam types them. There is no "save" button, every keystroke is already saved, and everyone in the doc sees the same text.

entries.caption: Sam finishes typing. Their paragraph is at the end of the doc.
On YOUR screen: Sam's paragraph appeared at the end of the doc, with no action from you. The avatar in the topbar tells you who.

entries.text: Sam leaves a comment for you

Sam highlights the line you wrote and leaves a thought. The comment thread appears in your sidebar within a second; the anchored passage gets a yellow underline. You can reply inline: same thread, no email loop, no Slack tab-switch.

entries.caption: Sam posts the comment. The thread sits in their sidebar.
On YOUR screen: Sam's comment lands in your sidebar, anchored to the line you wrote. Reply inline; the conversation lives with the doc.
